They exist so the mailbox route (Route B in monitor/collectors/govwales.py) can be exercised end-to-end without a live Microsoft 365 tenant, because gov.wales blocks direct HTTP access from cloud hosts. The content is NOT invented: every item below is a real Welsh Government publication, sourced either from the Camlas W29 briefing of 17 July 2026 or from gov.wales itself. Titles, dates and closing dates are reproduced as published. Delete this file before go-live.
subject: Consultation: Implementing the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026

body.content:
We want your views on how we implement the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026, including the remediation regulations, protections for leaseholders, and how building height and storeys are measured.

The Act creates an occupation-phase fire and structural safety regime for regulated buildings of at least 11 metres or five storeys, designates local authorities as building safety authorities, and empowers the Residential Property Tribunal to make remediation orders and remediation contribution orders.

Proposed leaseholder protections include no charge where the landlord is responsible for the defect, caps for landlords with net worth over £2m, no charges on leases valued under £175,000, and full protection from cladding remediation costs.

This consultation closes on 7 September 2026.

Read the consultation: https://www.gov.wales/implementing-building-safety-wales-act-2026-html

subject: Consultation: Council Tax Reduction Scheme in Wales - technical consultation on reassessment thresholds

body.content:
We want your views on the changes we want to make to the Council Tax Reduction Scheme in Wales.

The technical consultation covers reassessment thresholds and how changes in a household's circumstances trigger a reassessment of entitlement.

Read the consultation: https://www.gov.wales/council-tax-reduction-scheme-wales-technical-consultation-reassessment-thresholds

subject: Consultation: New tax rules for second homes and self-catering accommodation

body.content:
The Welsh Government has launched a 12-week consultation on reducing the 182-day actual-letting threshold that self-catering properties must meet to be liable for non-domestic rates rather than council tax. The current test requires a property to be available to let for 252 days and actually let for 182 days.

Five possible new exemptions are proposed: properties that form part of a wider business; large multi-unit properties; properties subject to planning restrictions; properties within the curtilage of the owner's own residence; and properties on the owner's farm.

Read more: https://www.gov.wales/new-tax-rules-second-homes

subject: Written Statement: Outcome of the First Supplementary Budget 2026-2027

body.content:
Elin Jones MS, Cabinet Minister for Finance.

Today, the Senedd voted against the Welsh Government's First Supplementary Budget for 2026-2027. This outcome is deeply disappointing. The Budget would have provided an additional £433 million of investment to support key public services and deliver commitments to the people of Wales. It contained no reductions to existing services and was focused on directing additional funding to areas facing significant pressure.

Read the statement: https://www.gov.wales/written-statement-outcome-first-supplementary-budget-2026-2027

_comment: Source: Camlas W29 briefing headline and gov.wales press release of 14 July 2026. This is the single most important item for the NRLA in the period.
subject: New Welsh Government announces its first phase of legislation

body.content:
The First Minister Rhun ap Iorwerth will set out the first phase of the Welsh Government's new legislative programme in a statement to the Senedd this afternoon.

The programme includes legislation to strengthen the rights of tenants in the private rented sector, initially focusing on strengthening the enforcement framework and the regulatory role of Rent Smart Wales, as well as requiring the sharing of rent data. This will lay the groundwork for more substantial changes to improve housing affordability, make rent fairer and limit no fault evictions later in the Senedd term. The Welsh Government is also developing proposals to legislate for the Right to Adequate Housing, and will proceed with a community right to buy scheme.

Read the announcement: https://www.gov.wales/new-welsh-government-announces-its-first-phase-of-legislation
